I want a deeper version of this task, not a bigger one. Before rewriting it, do four things:

1. Say what a top professional in this field would do here that I'm not asking for.
2. Name the rawest material they would start from instead of what has already been digested for me.
3. Name the specific methods and tools they would use.
4. Say what, other than you or me, would show the result is right.

Then rewrite my prompt to ask for exactly that.

<timestamp>Saturday, Nov 7, 2026, 4:23 PM (UTC)</timestamp>
<user_query>
/sharpen Investigate why a command-line application sometimes loses the last line of output when it exits.
</user_query>

1. A top systems engineer would isolate whether loss occurs in the application, runtime buffering, shell pipeline, PTY, or output-capture layer—and build a minimal deterministic reproduction.

2. They would start from raw stdout/stderr bytes, process lifecycle events, system-call traces, exit status, source code around shutdown, and the exact execution environment—not summarized logs.

3. They would use repeated controlled runs, pipe-versus-PTY comparisons, byte-level output comparison, shutdown-path inspection, and syscall tracing with the platform-appropriate tool (`dtruss`, `strace`, or equivalent).

4. Correctness would be demonstrated by an automated regression test that captures the exact expected bytes across repeated runs and relevant execution modes, supported by traces showing whether the final write reaches the OS before process termination.

Rewritten prompt:

> Investigate why this command-line application intermittently loses its final output line on exit. Build the smallest reliable reproduction and determine which layer drops the data: application logic, language/runtime buffering, shutdown handling, stdout/stderr redirection, shell pipelines, PTY behavior, or the output-capture system.
>
> Work from the application source, raw captured stdout/stderr bytes, process exit status, exact runtime environment, and platform-level write/exit traces. Compare relevant execution modes—such as interactive terminal, PTY, redirected file, and pipe—using repeated controlled runs and byte-level output comparisons.
>
> Identify the causal mechanism with evidence, then propose the narrowest fix. Validate it with an automated regression test that checks the exact output over enough repetitions to expose the intermittent failure, plus syscall or equivalent tracing that confirms the final bytes are written before exit.
>
> Leave open for me to choose the supported platforms, required execution modes, acceptable fix location, and repetition threshold.
